mainEntity.name: Can one of these bots accidentally publish, email, or spend money without me noticing?

acceptedAnswer.text: Keep human approval before a bot sends messages, publishes content, spends money, changes customer records, or signs up for services. A prompt can describe a safeguard, but the actual protection also depends on account permissions, platform settings, integrations, and how the workflow is monitored. Use draft-only access where possible, separate research from action, and require a clear approval status before consequential steps. Maintain an activity log showing the input, output, reviewer, decision, and any correction. Start with low-risk internal tasks before testing customer-facing or financial workflows. Recheck permissions whenever the workflow, platform, or team changes. Run My AI Biz describes human-directed automation as a core principle rather than presenting unattended execution as a default.
acceptedAnswer.description: It can if the workflow and connected accounts allow unsupervised actions. Begin with draft-only permissions, approval checkpoints, separate research from execution, and activity logs. Require explicit confirmation before publication, outreach, purchases, account changes, or customer-record updates, and review permissions whenever the setup changes.
